Shape equations

Heart hiccups

x = 3sin³θ
y = (13cosθ−5cos2θ−2cos3θ−cos4θ)/5.8+0.35

Equation and sound mapping

A trigonometric heart outline. Four laps, paired heartbeat attacks and a shorter high chirp. Pitch follows the vertical outline; this is not an ECG model. For scan progress t=0…1, θ=2π frac(4t), unless the shape uses explicit strokes. Sound pitch height=0.65y(t); horizontal position controls the stated timbre. Root=146.832 Hz. Amplitude clock=24t, r=frac(clock); gains=(1,0.75,0,1,0.55,0), gate=0.74, decay=3. Envelope=gain*min(1,r/0.045)*exp(−decay*r)*clamp((gate−r)/0.055,0,1); pen lifts are silent. Vivid uses the stated synthesis; Original retains its legacy voice mapping.

Star cartwheel

Pᵢ = rᵢ(cosαᵢ,sinαᵢ)
rᵢ = 3 (i even), 1.25 (i odd)

Equation and sound mapping

αᵢ=π/2+2πi/10, i=0…9. Linearly interpolate consecutive vertices and close the polygon. Five laps; each point gets a bright attack and each valley a softer reply. For scan progress t=0…1, θ=2π frac(5t), unless the shape uses explicit strokes. Sound pitch height=0.65y(t); horizontal position controls the stated timbre. Root=164.814 Hz. Amplitude clock=50t, r=frac(clock); gains=(1,0.35), gate=0.8, decay=2.8. Envelope=gain*min(1,r/0.045)*exp(−decay*r)*clamp((gate−r)/0.055,0,1); pen lifts are silent. Vivid uses the stated synthesis; Original retains its legacy voice mapping.

Smiley giggles

Face: x=2.8cosθ, y=2.8sinθ
Eyes: radius 0.23; smile: radius 1.65

Equation and sound mapping

Four strokes: face circle; circles centered at (−0.95,0.85) and (0.95,0.85); smile arc centered at (0,0.1), angles 1.15π…1.85π. Equal stroke time, with the last 4% of each interval lifting the pen. Three laps, short laughing pulses. For scan progress t=0…1, θ=2π frac(3t), unless the shape uses explicit strokes. Sound pitch height=0.65y(t); horizontal position controls the stated timbre. Root=130.813 Hz. Amplitude clock=48t, r=frac(clock); gains=(1,0.65,0.8,0), gate=0.62, decay=3.5. Envelope=gain*min(1,r/0.045)*exp(−decay*r)*clamp((gate−r)/0.055,0,1); pen lifts are silent. Vivid uses the stated synthesis; Original retains its legacy voice mapping.

Flower fizz

r = 2.9cos5θ
x = r cosθ; y = r sinθ

Equation and sound mapping

Five-petal polar rose. Three full angular laps (each traces every petal twice). Ten fizzy attacks per lap; FM brightness follows sideways distance. For scan progress t=0…1, θ=2π frac(3t), unless the shape uses explicit strokes. Sound pitch height=0.65y(t); horizontal position controls the stated timbre. Root=195.998 Hz. Amplitude clock=30t, r=frac(clock); gains=(1,0.5,1,0.7,0), gate=0.77, decay=2.4. Envelope=gain*min(1,r/0.045)*exp(−decay*r)*clamp((gate−r)/0.055,0,1); pen lifts are silent. Vivid uses the stated synthesis; Original retains its legacy voice mapping.

Butterfly blips

r = 0.85[e^(cosθ)−2cos4θ+sin⁵(θ/12)]
x = r sinθ; y = r cosθ−0.5

Equation and sound mapping

One-turn segment of the Fay butterfly curve, repeated four times. The classical full curve uses a longer parameter interval; this one-turn segment emphasizes the wing silhouette. Fluttering amplitude alternates rapid paired notes and rests. For scan progress t=0…1, θ=2π frac(4t), unless the shape uses explicit strokes. Sound pitch height=0.65y(t); horizontal position controls the stated timbre. Root=196.000 Hz. Amplitude clock=48t, r=frac(clock); gains=(1,0.6,0,1,0.6,0), gate=0.65, decay=2. Envelope=gain*min(1,r/0.045)*exp(−decay*r)*clamp((gate−r)/0.055,0,1); pen lifts are silent. Vivid uses the stated synthesis; Original retains its legacy voice mapping.

Moon mischief

Outer: x=2.9cosθ, y=2.9sinθ
Inner: x=2.7−√(R²−y²)

Equation and sound mapping

Outer arc: θ=π/3…5π/3. Inner arc goes bottom to top, y=−2.9sin(π/3)…2.9sin(π/3); R=sqrt(1.25²+(2.9sin(π/3))²). Two strokes with 4% pen lifts. Three laps. Low scoops alternate with silvery chirps; ring frequency follows horizontal position. For scan progress t=0…1, θ=2π frac(3t), unless the shape uses explicit strokes. Sound pitch height=0.65y(t); horizontal position controls the stated timbre. Root=98.000 Hz. Amplitude clock=24t, r=frac(clock); gains=(1,0,0.7,0.4,1,0,0.5,0), gate=0.86, decay=1.7. Envelope=gain*min(1,r/0.045)*exp(−decay*r)*clamp((gate−r)/0.055,0,1); pen lifts are silent. Vivid uses the stated synthesis; Original retains its legacy voice mapping.

Spiral slinky

r = 0.25+2.65v; θ=6πv
x = r cosθ; y = r sinθ

Equation and sound mapping

v runs from 0 to 1 and back within each lap. Three laps. Each outward journey builds a chirping register; the return collapses it. Amplitude pulses accelerate outward with clock c=12v+12v² and reverse inward. For scan progress t=0…1, θ=2π frac(3t), unless the shape uses explicit strokes. Sound pitch height=0.65y(t); horizontal position controls the stated timbre. Root=164.814 Hz. Amplitude clock=12v+12v², r=frac(clock); gains=(1,0.65,1,0), gate=0.78, decay=2.4. Envelope=gain*min(1,r/0.045)*exp(−decay*r)*clamp((gate−r)/0.055,0,1); pen lifts are silent. Vivid uses the stated synthesis; Original retains its legacy voice mapping.

References

  • Wolfram Function Repository: RoseCurveAnalysis - Polar rose geometry used in Flower fizz.
  • Paul Bourke: Butterfly curve, attributed to Temple Fay - One-turn butterfly segment; the full classical curve uses a longer interval.
  • Barry Truax: FM synthesis - Harmonic and inharmonic timbre construction.

All arrangements, rhythm windows and geometry-to-sound mappings are original. Shapes are parametric paths rather than single-valued y(x) graphs. The cursor follows the outline; vertical position sets pitch and the specified horizontal controls change timbre. Drawing uses equal x/y scale. All 123 earlier patterns remain.
